1. Formatting Cells

Cell formatting alters how data is displayed without changing the underlying stored value.

A. The "Format Cells" Central Hub

  • Keyboard Shortcut: Ctrl + 1 (Windows) or Cmd + 1 (macOS).
  • Opens the comprehensive formatting dialogue with six tabs: Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill, and Protection.

B. Core Formatting Dimensions

                    ┌────────────── FORMATTING DIMENSIONS ──────────────┐
                    │                                                   │
             Typography & Style                  Alignment & Layout             Borders & Fills
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐           ┌───────────┴───────────┐      ┌──────────┴──────────┐
      Font        Weight       Color      Horizontal    Vertical    Wrap  Border Style   Fill Shading
     Family       Size       Effects     Alignment    Alignment   Text    Line Color     Gradients

  1. Font Formatting:

    • Attributes: Typeface (e.g., Aptos, Calibri, Arial), font size, font color, bold (Ctrl + B), italic (Ctrl + I), and underline (Ctrl + U).
    • Special Typography: Strikethrough (for completed tasks), Superscript ($X^2$), and Subscript ($H_2O$) available within Ctrl + 1.

  2. Alignment & Orientation:

    • Horizontal Alignment: Left (default for text), Center, Right (default for numbers), and Justify.
    • Vertical Alignment: Top, Center, or Bottom of the cell.
    • Orientation (Text Rotation): Slants text counterclockwise, clockwise, or vertically. Ideal for labeling narrow columns to save horizontal screen real estate.

  3. Text Control Options:

    • Wrap Text (Alt + H + W): Displays multi-line text within a single cell when the text exceeds column width, increasing row height automatically.
    • Shrink to Fit: Automatically scales down the visual font size so data fits within current column boundaries without altering column width (does not change the actual font point size setting).
    • Merge & Center: Combines multiple adjacent cells into one large cell and centers the contents.
      • Best Practice Warning: Avoid merging cells inside raw data ranges; it breaks column sorting, filtering, and VBA selections.
      • Safer Alternative: Use "Center Across Selection" (found under Ctrl + 1 $\rightarrow$ Alignment $\rightarrow$ Horizontal). It centers the title visually across selected columns without merging cell boundaries.

  4. Borders and Fill Shading:

    • Borders: Add visual grid structure for printing (default worksheet gridlines do not always print). Customize border weight, line style (dashed, double-line for accounting totals), and border line colors.
    • Fills: Applies solid background colors, pattern fills, or two-color gradient fills to highlight headers, summary rows, or alert areas.

2. Defining and Using Styles

A Cell Style is a predefined set of formatting attributes (font, font size, number format, cell borders, and cell shading) saved under a single name.

A. Benefits of Styles

  • Consistency: Enforces a unified visual standard across corporate financial reports and workbooks.
  • Efficiency: Applies complex multi-attribute formatting (e.g., 12pt Bold Aptos, Currency format, top border, double-underline bottom border) in a single click.
  • Global Updates: Modifying a defined style automatically updates every cell in the workbook linked to that style.

B. Built-in Cell Styles (Home Tab $\rightarrow$ Cell Styles)

  • Good, Bad, and Neutral: Green (Good/Passed), Red (Bad/Failed), Yellow (Neutral/Warning).
  • Data and Model: Specific styles for Input cells (orange/peach unshaded), Calculation cells, Notes, and Output.
  • Titles and Headings: Pre-scaled hierarchical typography (Title, Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3).
  • Number Formats: Instant styling for Comma, Currency, and Percent.

C. Creating, Modifying, and Merging Styles

  1. Create Style from an Existing Cell:
    • Format a cell with your desired font, colors, borders, and number formats.
    • Go to Home $\rightarrow$ Cell Styles $\rightarrow$ click New Cell Style...
    • Name the style (e.g., Corporate_Header) $\rightarrow$ check the formatting properties you want included $\rightarrow$ click OK.
  2. Modifying an Existing Style:
    • Right-click the style in the Cell Styles gallery $\rightarrow$ click Modify... $\rightarrow$ adjust settings. All cells formatted with this style update dynamically across the workbook.
  3. Merging Styles from Another Workbook:
    • Open both the source workbook (containing custom styles) and the target workbook.
    • In the target workbook: Go to Home $\rightarrow$ Cell Styles $\rightarrow$ click Merge Styles... $\rightarrow$ select the open source workbook.

3. Workbook Themes and Table Styles

While Cell Styles format individual cells, Themes and Table Styles format the document globally.

┌──────────────────────────────── WORKBOOK THEME ────────────────────────────────┐
│ Applies document-wide across all worksheets, charts, shapes, and tables        │
│                                                                                │
│   ┌─────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────┐  │
│   │    Theme Colors     │   │     Theme Fonts     │   │    Theme Effects    │  │
│   │ 4 Text/Background   │   │  Heading Font       │   │ Visual styling for  │  │
│   │ 6 Accent Colors     │   │  Body Font          │   │ shapes, charts, and │  │
│   │ 2 Hyperlink Colors  │   │                     │   │ smart art objects   │  │
│   └─────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────┘  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

A. Workbook Themes (Page Layout Tab)

A Theme is a universal palette comprising three coordinated design elements:

  1. Colors: 12 specific color swatches (4 for text and backgrounds, 6 accent colors for charts and tables, and 2 for hyperlinks).
  2. Fonts: A paired set of typography—one font for Headings and one for Body text (e.g., Aptos Display / Aptos or Calibri Light / Calibri).
  3. Effects: Pre-set line styles, shadows, and 3D visual treatments applied to graphic shapes and charts.
  • Switching Themes: Changing the Theme (e.g., from Office to Facet or Slate) dynamically shifts all colors, table headers, and fonts across every sheet without needing manual re-formatting.
  • Standard Colors vs. Theme Colors:
    • Theme Colors adjust automatically when the theme changes.
    • Standard Colors (fixed red, dark blue, yellow, etc.) remain static regardless of theme shifts.

B. Table Styles (Table Design Tab)

When a range is converted into an official Table (Ctrl + T), dedicated Table Styles control its appearance:

  • Categorized into Light, Medium, and Dark designs.
  • Table Style Options (Checkboxes):
    • Header Row: Distinct styling/shading for column headers.
    • Total Row: Displays bold bottom-border accounting styling.
    • Banded Rows / Banded Columns: Alternates colors between consecutive rows/columns to prevent eye-tracking errors across wide tables.
    • First / Last Column: Applies unique bold formatting to highlight key identifier columns or end-line totals.
  • Creating a Custom Table Style: Right-click an existing table style $\rightarrow$ choose Duplicate... $\rightarrow$ customize individual components (such as Whole Table, First Row Stripe, or Header Row).

4. Making Numbers Easier to Read

Raw numbers (e.g., 1234567.891) are difficult to read and interpret. Number formatting introduces structure (commas, currency symbols, fixed decimal places) without altering mathematical precision.

A. Core Number Formats

Format Raw Stored Data Displayed Output Distinct Characteristic
General 1250.5 1250.5 Default unformatted representation; displays as entered.
Number 1250.5 1,250.50 User defines fixed decimal places and toggles $1,000$ separator ,.
Currency 1250.5 $1,250.50 Currency symbol placed immediately flush against the first digit.
Accounting 1250.5 $ 1,250.50 Currency symbol pinned to the far left; decimals align vertically; zeros display as a dash (-).
Percentage 0.155 15.50% Multiplies stored value by $100$ and appends a % sign.
Date 46277 09/12/2026 Converts serial integer numbers to calendar dates.

Accounting vs. Currency:
Financial models favor Accounting format because it vertically aligns decimal points and currency symbols, and replaces distracting zeros ($0.00) with a clean dash (-).

B. Custom Number Formatting Syntax

Accessed via Ctrl + 1 $\rightarrow$ Number tab $\rightarrow$ Custom.
Excel interprets custom formats through up to four sections separated by semicolons:

$$\mathbf{\text{POSITIVE}} ;;; \mathbf{\text{NEGATIVE}} ;;; \mathbf{\text{ZERO}} ;;; \mathbf{\text{TEXT}}$$

#,##0.00;[Red](#,##0.00);"-";@

Syntax Key & Placeholders:

  • 0 (Digit Placeholder): Displays nonsignificant zeros if the number has fewer digits than specified (e.g., format 0.00 turns 5 into 5.00).
  • # (Digit Placeholder): Displays only significant digits; suppresses leading/trailing zeros (e.g., format #.## turns 5 into 5).
  • ? (Alignment Placeholder): Adds non-printing spaces for insignificant zeros to ensure decimal points align when using non-proportional fonts.
  • , (Thousands Separator or Scaling Factor):
    • Between digits: #,##0 adds standard commas (1,000,000).
    • At the end: Scales by thousands. Format #,##0, "K" displays 50,000 as 50 K. Format #,##0.0,, "M" displays 2,500,000 as 2.5 M.
  • @ (Text Placeholder): Represents where text entered in the cell will display.
  • Color Identifiers: Placed in square brackets at the start of a section (e.g., [Red], [Green], [Blue]).

5. Changing Appearance Based on Value (Conditional Formatting)

Conditional Formatting changes the visual style of a cell (fill, font color, borders) dynamically based on conditions or evaluations.

                    ┌──────────── CONDITIONAL FORMATTING MODES ────────────┐
                    │                                                      │
             Rule-Based Triggers                               Visual Data Representation
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐                      ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
  Highlight Rules         Top/Bottom Rules          Data Bars         Color Scales         Icon Sets
  (>, <, =, Between,      (Top 10%, Above Avg,     (In-cell mini      (Heatmaps: 2-color  (Indicators: arrows,
   Text Contains)          Bottom 10 Items)         bar graphics)      or 3-color bands)   flags, traffic lights)

A. Pre-built Rule Types

  1. Highlight Cells Rules:
    • Flags values: Greater Than, Less Than, Between, Equal To, Text that Contains, A Date Occurring, or Duplicate Values.
  2. Top / Bottom Rules:
    • Identifies upper or lower tiers: Top 10 Items, Top 10%, Bottom 10 Items, Bottom 10%, Above Average, or Below Average.
  3. Data Bars:
    • Inserts colored horizontal bars inside cells. Length represents cell value relative to the rest of the range (acts as an in-cell micro bar chart).
  4. Color Scales (Heatmaps):
    • Uses 2-color or 3-color gradients (e.g., Green-Yellow-Red) where shading indicates high, mid-tier, and low data distribution.
  5. Icon Sets:
    • Adds indicator symbols (directional arrows, traffic lights, flags, checkmarks/crosses) classified by user-defined percentiles or hard values.

B. Custom Formula Rules (Highlighting Entire Rows)

To apply formatting to an entire record (row) based on the value of a single column cell, use a custom logical formula:

  1. Select the entire table data range (e.g., A2:E50).
  2. Go to Conditional Formatting $\rightarrow$ New Rule... $\rightarrow$ select "Use a formula to determine which cells to format".
  3. Type the formula using a mixed cell reference (lock the column with $, leave the row relative):
    =$E2="Overdue"
  4. Choose the formatting (e.g., light red fill) $\rightarrow$ click OK.
    Result: Whenever the status in column E reads "Overdue", the entire corresponding row ($A$ through $E$) turns light red.

C. The Conditional Formatting Rules Manager

  • Located at: Home $\rightarrow$ Conditional Formatting $\rightarrow$ Manage Rules...
  • Displays all active rules across the current selection or the entire worksheet.
  • Features:
    • Adjust rule evaluation hierarchy (up/down priority arrows).
    • Edit rule conditions and formatting styles.
    • Adjust the range of cells to which the rule applies (Applies to field).
    • Stop If True Checkbox: Halts evaluation of subsequent rules for a cell if the current rule evaluates to true.

6. Adding and Formatting Images in Worksheets

Spreadsheets can incorporate corporate branding (logos), product photos, and explanatory diagrams.

A. Inserting Images

  • Go to the Insert tab $\rightarrow$ Illustrations $\rightarrow$ Pictures:
    • This Device: Inserts local graphics files (.png, .jpg, .svg).
    • Stock Images: Inserts royalty-free images from Microsoft's built-in library.
    • Online Pictures: Searches web sources (Bing).

B. "Place in Cell" vs. "Place Over Cells"

  • Place Over Cells (Traditional): The image floats on top of the worksheet canvas as a free-floating object.
  • Place in Cell: Embeds the image directly inside the cell grid itself.
    • The image behaves like standard cell data.
    • It stays locked within the cell, resizes when rows/columns change, sorts with the data, and filters seamlessly without drifting across the screen.

C. Formatting and Manipulating Graphic Objects

When a floating image is selected, the Picture Format contextual tab appears:

  • Sizing & Cropping: Use the Crop tool to remove unwanted margins. Hold Shift while dragging corner sizing handles to preserve the original Aspect Ratio (preventing distortion).
  • Color & Contrast: Adjust Brightness, Sharpness, Contrast, or convert to Grayscale.
  • Remove Background: Automatically detects and strips solid background colors from company logos.
  • Compress Pictures: Reduces the image resolution (e.g., for Web, Print, or Email) to lower overall workbook file size.

D. Object Placement Properties

Right-click image $\rightarrow$ select Format Picture... $\rightarrow$ open Size & Properties tab $\rightarrow$ expand Properties:

                       ┌───────── OBJECT PLACEMENT PROPERTIES ─────────┐
                       │                                               │
           Move and size with cells       Move but don't size with cells      Don't move or size with cells
           • Columns widen = Pic widens   • Row deleted = Pic shifts position • Stays completely static
           • Ideal for product catalogs   • Size remains constant             • Ideal for floating logos
  1. Move and size with cells: If rows or columns behind the picture are inserted, deleted, expanded, or filtered, the picture resizes and shifts accordingly.
  2. Move but don't size with cells: If rows/columns are inserted or hidden above/left of the image, it shifts position to stay with adjacent data, but its dimensions (height and width) remain static.
  3. Don't move or size with cells: The image remains fixed in place on the screen regardless of structural grid adjustments.
